A1.justification: Both PDFs describe successive versions of the same camera-ray-conditioned monocular reconstruction work, expanded from MetricHMR to MetricHMSR. Text, equations, tables and figures support comparison throughout. v1 has no appendix; v2 includes readable Supplementary Material, Sections 6–8.

before.justification: v1 reports original human-pose and trajectory evaluations, a pose-ambiguity experiment, and a camera-ray ablation, including Tables 2–5.

after.justification: v2 reports original pose, trajectory, focal-length robustness and depth-estimation results, together with component ablations and expert-routing analyses in the main text and supplement.

M1.justification: v1's concatenated image/ray features and iterative MLP regressor become Patch and Global Human MoE with routed, shared and ray experts. v2 adds explicit 3D-joint, vertex, height and load-balancing losses. It also introduces mesh-guided UNet–ViT depth refinement over MapAnything, substantially extending v1's human reconstruction and UniDepth point-cloud overlay pipeline.

E1.justification: The reported training mix replaces Human3.6M and MPI-INF with BEDLAM, AIC, COCO and MPII, retaining 3DPW. Static-camera trajectory evaluation changes from Human3.6M to RICH. v2 adds PROX depth training/evaluation and SynFocal evaluation under varying focal lengths. Local-pose evaluation on 3DPW/EMDB-1 and trajectory evaluation on EMDB-2 remain.

E2.justification: The matched local-pose comparison adds PersPose, Human3R, CameraHMR and PromptHMR, while removing SPIN, CLIFF, ReFit and TRACE. EMDB-2 comparisons expand to additional methods including PromptHMR-vid, TRACE, GLAMR, SLAHMR and Human3R, with membership depending on camera settings. New depth comparisons evaluate Metric3D, UniDepth and MapAnything; SynFocal compares against Human3R.

E3.justification: Although AdamW, 40 epochs and batch size 64 remain, weight decay changes from 0.01 to 0.0001, and differentiated learning rates become a stated uniform 0.00001. New protocols include a 9:1 PROX train/test split with AbsRel, MAE and delta1 evaluation, and controlled focal-length variation assessed with RPSD and RDE. Existing pose and trajectory metrics remain.

E4.justification: v1's Bbox+K versus ray ablation on 3DPW/Human3.6M is replaced by image-only, added-ray and added-MoE comparisons on 3DPW/EMDB-2. v2 adds focal-length robustness tests and expert-routing analyses by body region, bounding-box scale and dataset. Conversely, v1's height-conditioned pose/depth ambiguity experiment in Section 3.2 and Figure 4 is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. v2's RPSD measures positional dispersion across focal-length conditions; it is a robustness metric rather than uncertainty reporting for estimated performance.

E6.justification: Under revised architecture and training, reported 3DPW PA-MPJPE/MPJPE/PVE changes from 37.5/60.5/72.1 to 33.6/53.0/62.7; these are not controlled same-setting gains. EMDB-2 ground-truth-camera ERVE instead rises from 8.9 to 9.4. New results include PROX MAE 0.46 versus MapAnything's 0.58 and SynFocal RPSD 1.1 cm versus Human3R's 21.6 cm. v2's HMR2.0a row also reproduces v1's SPIN 3DPW triplet without explaining the attribution.

T1.justification: The documented cropped-intrinsic equation is corrected: v1 Equation 4 subtracts crop offsets from focal lengths, whereas v2 Equation 2 subtracts them from principal-point coordinates. v2 also introduces short mathematical definitions for expert balancing, depth correction and RPSD/RDE. These are limited formal additions and corrections, without a substantial theorem or proof development.

C1.justification: The central contribution expands from metric human shape, pose and position recovery to joint human/scene reconstruction and pseudo-ground-truth annotation. Human MoE, human-guided depth refinement and SynFocal become explicit contributions. v1's claim of requiring no 3D training supervision disappears. v2's conclusion qualifies its overall superiority claim to online single-frame methods.

C2.justification: v2 introduces substantive mechanism explanations based on semantic expert specialization, global routing, redundant supervision and mesh-anchored depth calibration. v1's discussion of nonunique metric solutions and its UniDepth-failure caveat disappear. v2 instead identifies heavy occlusion as a limitation and acknowledges keypoint/patch limitations in routing analysis. These change both the interpretation and stated applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands implementation documentation: named encoders, expert configuration, 256-by-256 crops, one A100 GPU, SynFocal construction, and detailed depth-refinement architecture, anchor filtering, normalization and affine constraints. These are disclosures, not evidence that every corresponding setting changed. Some specificity is lost: v1 explicitly identifies Masked-DROID for its trajectory evaluation, while v2 does not specify its corresponding extrinsic-estimation procedure.

R1.justification: Research positioning expands to MoE specialization and joint human-scene reconstruction, incorporating DeepSeekMoE, VIMoE, VGGT, MapAnything, CUT3R and Human3R, alongside newer perspective-aware HMR methods. v2 explicitly credits NeRF-inspired camera rays and recognizes CLIFF's full-perspective projection usage. This substantially revises v1's predominantly camera-model and metric-depth framing.

P1.justification: The title and author information change, and the abstract, introduction, related work, method and conclusion are extensively rewritten around MetricHMSR. The standalone Metric Pose Bias section disappears, with its camera explanations transferred to supplementary implementation material. A substantial supplement organizes implementation, additional results and limitations, changing the narrative structure beyond merely adding experiments.

P2.justification: The pipeline is redrawn with MoE and depth-refinement branches, accompanied by new expert diagrams, routing plots, SynFocal examples and positional-distribution graphics. EMDB results are split into predicted/ground-truth-camera tables with online/offline groups. Original camera illustrations largely reappear as Figures 9–11, and COCO overlays are reused in Figure 14; these are relocations, not wholly new evidence.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens assessment of the central metric-reconstruction claims: it corrects the cropped-camera equation, adds controlled focal-length tests and staged component ablations, and quantitatively evaluates scene depth where v1 mainly showed overlays. Expanded implementation details and stronger comparison methods further improve assessability. Removing the ambiguity discussion and leaving the HMR2.0a/SPIN score overlap unexplained are weaknesses, but the targeted validation and mathematical correction provide a substantial net improvement. Higher cross-version scores alone do not establish this judgment.
